An accelerating obby is common on Roblox and reads as Infinite Runner until you notice the player still controls their own movement. The boundary note covers auto-run versus own-pace, but not the case where the pace is the player's and the speed is not.

notes_for_us: Three-faction territorial warfare has no representation. spawn-teambase is written for two teams at opposite ends, and there is no option for a contested holding whose ownership persists. capture-zone is a bomb site; a keep that one realm owns until another takes it is a different thing, and this prompt is built entirely around them.

The prompt is mostly an engineering spec - determinism, RNG, tick order, networking, persistence - and layout-intake has no way to acknowledge a constraint set that governs how everything is produced. Every visible object must come from generate_mesh is a hard rule over the whole build and it ended up nowhere.
Ten zones across three realms is the largest P4 I have emitted, and the handoff cannot say which zones are which map or what order they unlock in. pipeline: [P4] carries none of that structure.

notes_for_us: tile-grid is worded as evenly divided squares for trivia rounds and tile-drop games. It is the only board option in the system and it is now carrying a hex grid whose tiles differ in height and brightness, which is close to the opposite of evenly divided.

The prompt's strongest visual requirement - a player should know a hex's output by looking at it, without a legend - is a rule about how geometry encodes data. Nothing in the handoff can state that, so it survives only inside one option's text where the image model may or may not honour it.

SET was exactly right here and cheap to reach, but the shape question it depends on (does anyone walk on the board) is one the prompt never answers, and stage B tells me to decide it rather than ask. On a board game that decision changes whether the tiles are 4 studs or 40.
